messages:
Mia: FYI — several EU customers started getting 401s for signed webhook callbacks around 07:00 UTC this morning. Saw it in PagerDuty.
Devon: Confirmed. Spike in /v1/webhook/verify 401s at 06:58–07:05 UTC. Only affects requests signed with java-sdk v1.3.2 from a particular partner.
Samir: Quick log snippet from the verifier: `verify_error: signature verification failed (no matching key found for kid)` — but the kid is present in the token header.
Olivia: Could be our JWKS cache stale? I remember a rotation yesterday from partner-side. What’s our fetch policy currently?
Mia: JWKS fetcher TTL is 12h and we only refresh on schedule. We intentionally avoid fetching on every verification for perf.
Devon: Partner confirmed they rotated keys at 06:45 UTC. If our cache still had only the old set and the token used the new kid, verification would fail.
Samir: There's also a secondary repro: one customer had their VM's system clock jump forward ~10 minutes (cron NTP resync). That broke tokens with tight exp/nbf windows — verifier rejected with `exp < now`.
Devon: So two interacting things: (1) cache TTL preventing immediate discovery of new key, (2) clients with non-monotonic clocks causing short-lived tokens to be invalid.
Mia: Repro steps I used: 1) Configure a local signer with two keys; 2) rotate to new key; 3) immediately sign token with 30s TTL; 4) set verifier's system clock +11s and try verify with cached JWKS only — fail reliably.
Samir: Repro log block:
```
[2024-03-11T06:59:12Z] token.kid = "k_20240311_b"
[2024-03-11T06:59:12Z] jwks.cached_keys = ["k_20240310_a"]
[2024-03-11T06:59:12Z] verify_error = "no matching key"
[2024-03-11T06:59:21Z] verify_error = "token expired (exp < now)"
```
Olivia: Minimal mitigation ideas: - add 60s leeway for exp/nbf checks - fetch JWKS on kid-miss (async/blocking) - reduce TTL to 15m or implement stale-while-revalidate
Devon: Fetch-on-miss sounds reasonable but could blow up traffic if partner rotates a lot. Maybe fetch-backoff + cache-stampede protection.
Mia: For short term: enable 60s leeway in verifier and add a fetch-on-kid-miss path that will attempt one immediate refresh and retry verification.
Samir: Patch outline I proposed: - if kid not found in cache -> async fetch JWKS, but perform a blocking short fetch if token age < 120s, then retry. Also emit metric `jwks.fetch_on_kid_miss` and `jwt.retries_after_fetch`.
Olivia: For long term we should: - expose JWKS TTL per issuer in Console - allow partners to publish `last_rotation` metadata (optional) - add robust stale-while-revalidate + jittered refresh
Mia: Also need an incident note for CS: explain root cause (rotation + local clock jumps + our TTL) and tell partners to avoid <1min token TTLs during rotation windows.
Devon: Assigning follow-ups: @samir bump verifier leeway and implement single fetch-on-miss (urgent) — target patch today. @olivia reduce default TTL to 15m and add metrics dashboard tile. @mia coordinate CS message and postmortem.
sec-bot: New issue created: SEC-2024-422 — "JWKS cache + clock-jump causing ephemeral token failures" (https://redwood.internal/issue/SEC-2024-422).
Samir: I'll open a PR for the verifier patch (link forthcoming). Also adding unit tests that simulate clock skew + immediate rotation.
Mia: Thanks — please paste PR/notes here when ready. I'll prepare customer comms and the rollback steps (how to flip leeway off if it causes regressions). :thumbsup:
Olivia: One more note: add a health alert if jwks.fetch_on_kid_miss rate exceeds X/min — indicates partner churn or malicious high-rotation.
Mia: Agreed. Ok closing the loop after PRs land.
